messages.subject: Re: Problems with DSM analysis - analysis halted due to missing
parts:
On 04/10/2011 14:10, Eric Rexstad wrote:
> > Ainars:
> >
> > I suspect you have not unticked the box that tells Distance to tidy up
> > after itself by removing old objects from the R workspace. Most times
> > being tidy is useful, but in this instance, the DSM engine needs the
> > objects created by the MRDS engine.
> >
> > Navigate to Tools | Preferences | Analysis and make sure the two
> > tickboxes underneath the Image properties button are not checked (see
> > screen capture at
> > http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/ericr/software/screenshot.4.png)
> >
> > I hope that will solve your problem.
> >
> >
> > On 04/10/2011 13:29, Ainars Aunins wrote:
>> >> Dear colleagues,
>> >>
>> >> I have problems with DSM analysis and I did not find a similar case discussed here in the mailing list.
>> >> The execution of the analysis is halted when data object "ddf.1" or "ddf.any number" (depending which of the previous CDS, MCDS or MRDS analyses I have indicated as the fitted detection probability function) is not found. It seems that Distance has not written this data to the R analysis folder. Any ideas what could be the problem and what can I do to fix this?
>> >> (BTW, MRDS analyses, which also use R, run fine. So there should be no problem with R installation).
